headline: Jokic, Murray help Nuggets hand Pelicans a sixth straight loss
text: NEW ORLEANS -- — Nikola Jokic had 26 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists, Jamal Murray added 23 points, seven rebounds and nine assists, and the Denver Nuggets outlasted the New Orleans Pelicans 116-108 on Saturday night. Denver has won four of its last five games and moved to 3-0 against the Pelicans this season. New Orleans dropped its sixth consecutive contest, four of which have come at home. Jokic was on triple-double watch, shooting 9 of 14 from the field. Murray shot 9 of 16 and was a team-high +16. Zion Williamson led New Orleans with 24 points. Saddiq Bey added 16 points, and rookie guard Jaron Pierre Jr . scored 13 in 23 minutes after scoring 23 points for the G-League Laketown Squadron’s inaugural home game earlier Saturday afternoon. Jokic dictated play early, scoring nine points in the first quarter and entering halftime with 12 points, five rebounds and five assists. But New Orleans showed fight, with Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen combining for 16 points in the first half. The Pelicans trimmed Denver’s lead to one with 53 seconds left in the half on a Pierre layup, then two on a Karlo Matkovic 3-pointer late in the third quarter. Christian Braun had 17 points, seven rebounds and four steals for Denver. A spinning DeMar DeRozan jumper gave the Nuggets their largest lead of the night, 102-87, with 6:36 remaining. Yves Missi (knee) returned to the lineup for New Orleans on a minutes restriction, logging three points, eight rebounds and four blocks after missing the previous 10 games. Trey Murphy (knee) missed his fourth straight game. Dejounte Murray (ankle) missed his second consecutive game after requesting a trade from the Pelicans on Friday. Up next Nuggets: Host Phoenix on Monday night. Pelicans: Host Golden State on Monday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Tyrese Proctor has a triple-double as short-handed Cavaliers top Mavericks 127-117
text: CLEVELAND -- — Tyrese Proctor posted his first triple-double with 24 points, 11 rebounds and a career-best 10 assists in leading the short-handed Cleveland Cavaliers to a 127-117 victory over the Dallas Mavericks on Saturday night. Australia native Proctor became the first Cleveland player with a triple-double since Max Strus against Charlotte on April 14, 2024. The points and assists were new career-highs for Proctor, and he also matched his pro high in rebounds. The Cavaliers played without their entire usual starting lineup as Donovan Mitchell (left knee), James Harden (left calf), Evan Mobley (left big toe), Jarrett Allen (right knee) and Peyton Watson (right hamstring) were sidelined with injuries. Sixth man Sam Merrill (right hamstring) also was inactive. The Cavs ruled out all of their starters after travel delays following the nationwide ground stop on Friday and having to stay overnight in South Florida after a loss to the Miami Heat . Former Cleveland guard Kyrie Irving scored 20 of his 34 points in the third quarter for Dallas, while Cooper Flagg had 18 points and eight rebounds. Flagg hugged fellow 2025 draftee — and former college teammate — Proctor shortly after he earned his 10th assist on a pass to Mario Hezonja . Proctor buried back-to-back 3-pointers in the fourth to give Cleveland the largest lead of the evening at 113-91. Irving drained a long 3-pointer with 2:23 left to pull the Mavericks within 122-112, but missed a 31-footer on their next possession that could have brought them within seven. Irving, who made the go-ahead 3-pointer in winning Game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals for the Cavaliers, received the loudest ovation of any player when introduced. Hezonja scored 22 points, rookie Meleek Thomas had a season-high 20 points and Norchad Omier scored his first 13 points and grabbed eight rebounds off the bench for Cleveland. Up next Mavericks: At Boston on Sunday. Cavaliers: Host Chicago on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Antetokounmpo scores 34, Heat block 14 shots and roll past Pistons 137-117 for 4th straight win
text: MIAMI -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 34 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists, some of the spectacular variety, and the Miami Heat beat the Detroit Pistons 137-117 on Saturday night for their fourth straight win. Klay Thompson scored 26 points in his return from a sprained ankle and Bam Adebayo added 20 for the Heat. Davion Mitchell had 15 points and nine rebounds for Miami. Cade Cunningham had 33 points and eight assists for Detroit, which got 20 points and seven assists from Kevin Huerter . Miami had nine players record at least one block and finished with 14 as a team — one shy of the franchise record. The NBA record for players on the same team having at least one block in a game is 10, done twice — both by Golden State, first in 1991 and then again in 2016. The Heat team record for players with at least one block was eight, done on five occasions. Antetokounmpo finished a weekend where he scored 71 points in a two-day span, after finishing with 37 in Miami's win over Cleveland on Friday night. He also had a through-the-legs assist to Thompson for a 3-pointer in the opening quarter. It was one of six 3s on the night for Thompson, who is now 26 away from tying former Heat guard Ray Allen (2,973) for the third-most 3-pointers in NBA history. Miami won for the seventh time in its last nine games and became the fourth team in the last 25 seasons to start 0-4 but rally to a winning record at the 13-game mark. Sacramento (7-6) did it in 2022-23, Oklahoma City (8-5) did it in 2018-19 and Dallas (9-4) did it in 2006-07. It also matched the best nine-game stretch for the Heat since an 8-1 burst in November 2023. Up next Pistons: Visit San Antonio on Tuesday night. Heat: Host Houston on Monday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Cedric Coward has 23 points and 12 rebounds as Grizzlies beat Nets 129-110
text: MEMPHIS, Tenn. -- — Cedric Coward had 23 points and 12 rebounds and Taylor Hendricks scored a career-high 22 as Memphis built an early lead and defeated the Brooklyn Nets 129-110 on Saturday night. A night after a 142-111 victory over New Orleans featured 10 Memphis players reaching double figures, tying an NBA record, seven Grizzlies reached double figures against the Nets. Javon Small scored 19 and Cam Spencer finished with 17 and eight assists as Memphis won its third in the last four. Julius Randle lead Brooklyn with 22 points and Day’Ron Sharpe added 16 points and 11 rebounds as Brooklyn lost its third in the last four. Noah Clowney scored 15. Memphis built a 20-point first-half lead behind 3-point success and weathered a third quarter Brooklyn burst that cut the advantage to single digits. By early in the fourth quarter, Memphis had taken the lead back to 24. Both teams had to overcome travel issues out of New Orleans that plagued the country during Friday's grounding of planes. The Nets stayed over after playing New Orleans on Wednesday; the Grizzlies beat the Pelicans on Friday night. The teams arrived midday Saturday only hours before tipoff. That led to compressed game preparation. Then Brooklyn's leading scorer and rebounder Michael Porter Jr . was a late scratch for personal reasons, eliminating 21.5 points and 7.5 rebounds from the Nets arsenal. The Grizzlies were without starters Ty Jerome , the team's leading scorer, and center Zach Edey . Memphis built an early double-digit lead behind starting 9 of 11 from 3-point range. The Nets shooting would improve in the second quarter, but Spencer's 3-pointer as time expired in the second — their 13th of the half — gave Memphis a 71-54 lead at the break. Up next Nets: Host Philadelphia on Monday. Grizzlies: At Wahington on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Bulls overcome travel delay and injuries to beat the Timberwolves 117-106
text: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Norman Powell scored 23 points, Matas Buzelis added 18 points and nine rebounds, and the short-handed Chicago Bulls won for the second night in a row with a 117-106 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves on Saturday. Buddy Hield and Tre Jones each chipped in 16 points off the bench for the Bulls, who ended Minnesota's five-game winning streak convincingly. Chicago's travel to Minneapolis on Friday was delayed by the nationwide ground stop that impacted many flights across the country. That meant the Bulls didn't arrive to Minnesota until the day of the game Saturday after beating the Hawks in Chicago on Friday. The travel disruption didn't seem to impact the Bulls, nor did a limited roster. Rookie Caleb Wilson is out for an extended period with a fractured hand. Jalen Smith also missed Saturday's game with a hand injury, and center Nic Claxton was sidelined with a hamstring injury. Buzelis picked up the scoring in their absence with 14 first-half points. The Timberwolves missed their first 13 shots from 3-point range and finished 9 for 38. Minnesota was held to 17 points in the first quarter, its lowest-scoring quarter of the season. The Wolves failed to reach 110 points for the first time this season. Wolves guard Ayo Dosunmu had a big third quarter against his former team to help Minnesota claw back. Dosunmu scored 14 of his team-high 24 points in the period. LaMelo Ball added 19 points. Chicago had no problem scoring at the rim in the first half. The Bulls scored 30 points of their 58 first-half points in the paint and finished with 54 paint points for the game. The Bulls also connected on 7 of 15 shots from deep before halftime. Up next Bulls: Play at Cleveland on Monday. Timberwolves: Host Portland on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
